about.text: Caciocavallo is a type of pasta filata ('stretched-curd') cheese made out of sheep's or cow's milk. It is produced throughout southern Italy, particularly in the Apennine Mountains and in the Gargano peninsula. Shaped like a teardrop, it is similar in taste to the aged southern Italian provolone cheese, with a hard edible rind.

how.label: stretch, hang
how.text: Caciocavallo Silano is a cow's-milk pasta filata moulded by hand into a closed, smooth pear or oval, then tied in pairs and hung over poles to ripen; it firms from elastic to flaky and develops a straw-yellow rind.

steps.note: The milk is raw or thermised.
With calf rennet or kid rennet paste.

steps.name: cut
steps.note: The curd is broken to hazelnut size.
Natural whey starter is permitted, and the curd is soured until it can be stretched.
Stretched in hot water and closed by hand into an oval or cone of 1–2.5 kg.

steps.name: brine
steps.note: In brine, the time set by the weight.
Tied in pairs and hung on poles.
